channel.title: Signal Brief · Cloud & DevOps
channel.description: Signal Brief: the day in technology, in The Signal's own words. Every item is written from linked official sources and fact checked before publication.

item.title: Google hands gVisor and its agent stack to the CNCF
item.description: Google is donating gVisor, Agent Substrate and OpenRL to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, putting its AI agent infrastructure under neutral governance. gVisor, open sourced by Google in 2018, runs a lightweight kernel in user space to intercept system calls, adding isolation between containers and the host system, and is used by Anthropic and OpenAI to run untrusted code. Agent Substrate 1.0, now generally available on Google Kubernetes Engine, lets agents pause when idle and resume without rebuilding their runtime, while OpenRL coordinates reinforcement learning training on a user’s own Kubernetes setup. Why it matters for tech: Sandboxing is becoming core infrastructure for agents that run untrusted code, and neutral ownership is Google’s bid to make its stack the default.

item.title: Cursor will now publish AI built apps to a live URL
item.description: Cursor has added fully managed deployment, letting its cloud agents take an AI generated app from a description to a live, shareable web address without the user setting up infrastructure. Cursor handles hosting, database provisioning and sign in, runs security checks for exposed credentials and secrets before publishing, and builds on Vercel for Platforms. The feature is available on all paid Cursor plans with cloud agents enabled, and targets internal business apps as well as personal projects. Why it matters for tech: Coding tools are closing the gap between generating an app and shipping it, which makes deployment skill less of a gate for new builders.

item.title: Azure Front Door gains generally available post quantum TLS key exchange
item.description: Microsoft made configurable TLS key exchange policies generally available in Azure Front Door, including hybrid post quantum key exchange. The option is aimed at teams preparing for future cryptographic threats while keeping client compatibility. Why it matters for tech: Post quantum readiness is reaching production edge services, so teams can start the migration before quantum computers threaten current cryptography.

item.title: Google donates its agent runtime stack to the CNCF as Agent Substrate hits 1.0
item.description: Google donated three open source projects that started at Google, Agent Substrate, gVisor and OpenRL, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation after their acceptance into the CNCF Sandbox. Agent Substrate, which runs isolated agent environments, reached version 1.0 and is generally available on Google Kubernetes Engine, restoring idle agents in under 500 milliseconds at 10 times container density. Why it matters for tech: Agent infrastructure is getting the same neutral, open governance treatment Kubernetes got, so no single vendor controls how agents run at scale.

item.title: Google previews AlloyDB Express, a scale to zero PostgreSQL for developers and agents
item.description: Google has announced a preview of AlloyDB Express, a version of AlloyDB for PostgreSQL designed for rapid testing and prototyping. It offers instant provisioning and scale to zero, aimed at development pipelines and coding agents that need short lived databases. Why it matters for tech: Databases are being reshaped around agent driven development, where environments spin up and down in minutes.

item.title: Amazon S3 Tables can now migrate Hive tables to Iceberg for you
item.description: AWS has added managed migration from Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg in Amazon S3 Tables. AWS says existing datasets can be converted with no pipelines to build and no compute to provision, while production workloads keep running. Why it matters for tech: Iceberg has become the default table format for lakehouse data, and managed migration removes the main barrier to switching.

item.title: Azure previews an MCP gateway for its container application gateway
item.description: Microsoft has put an MCP gateway for Application Gateway for Containers into public preview, adding a Model Context Protocol route type. Platform teams can publish MCP servers behind one hostname while centralising TLS, token validation and firewall controls. Why it matters for tech: Gateways are becoming the control point where enterprises govern agent traffic.

item.title: Nammu21 runs syndicated loan automation on Google Cloud's ledger in a proof of concept
item.description: Fintech firm Nammu21 worked with Google Cloud to structure syndicated loan agreements as smart contracts on the Google Cloud Universal Ledger. The proof of concept automates the loan lifecycle in a market where settlement currently takes weeks of manual processing. Why it matters for tech: It tests ledger technology on a real, high value financial workflow rather than a pilot in isolation.

item.title: AWS makes Step Functions callable as agent tools
item.description: In its weekly roundup, AWS notes that Step Functions, its workflow service spanning more than 220 AWS services, can now be handed to AI agents as a tool. Workflows that teams already run and trust become callable by agents without being rewritten. Why it matters for tech: It shows cloud platforms adapting established automation for agents rather than replacing it.

item.title: Developers choose smaller AI models on purpose, and report better results
item.description: The New Stack reports that some development teams are deliberately downgrading the AI models they use for coding work, and finding the results better for their purposes. The smaller setups can be cheaper and easier to control for the tasks these teams run most. Why it matters for tech: Model choice is becoming an engineering decision about fit and cost, not a race to the most powerful model.
